chapter: Russell's band, records and Armstrong in the studio
title: Louis Metcalf's crown and Armstrong's high F at the Savoy
summary: Metcalf wore a crown as king of the band until Armstrong played a high F on a two-night Savoy visit and Teddy Hill threw the crown into the audience.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: But at the time you were at the Savoy, wasn't...?

Louis had a crown made. Louis Metcalf had a crown. He was the king. That's because Russell had so many show-stopping numbers we used to play, and naturally, we'd finish one of them numbers and the applause would bring the house down, as they say. Well, naturally, the trumpet player, he'd take the bow, you know -- because they played louder than anybody else. So that made him the King. Metcalf was the King, you know. He had his crown and everything.

So Louis Armstrong comes to New York for a two-day engagement at the Savoy, and he was playing in front Russell's band. So when Louis played his first number, he opened up and played the first number...
What was it? Do you remember the number?

I don't remember the opening number. But I know on the end of it he played a high F, which in them days, that had never been heard of before. And Louis hit that F, big and broad and loud and clear. And the house did come tumblin' down. That's when Teddy Hill got'up and turned around to Louis Metcalf, with that crown on his head, and snatched the crown off and threw it out in the audience! -- and said, "The King is now dethroned." Heh. "There's a new King. Long live the King." He was talkin' about Louis
